question:
Case Study:

A student solves the determinant $\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{vmatrix}=k$. Find the value of $k$. Also, confirm whether the system $2x + y - z = 2, x + y + z = 3, x + 2y + 3z = 5$ has a unique solution or not.
explanation:
Let $D = \begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{vmatrix}$

Expand:

$= 2\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{vmatrix} - 1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{vmatrix} + (-1)\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{vmatrix}$

First minor: $1\times3 - 1\times2 = 3 - 2 = 1$

Second: $1\times3 - 1\times1 = 3-1=2$

Third: $1\times2-1\times1=2-1=1$

$= 2(1) - 1(2) + (-1)(1) = 2 - 2 -1 = -1$

As $|A| = -1 \neq 0$, the system has a unique solution.

options.A: $k=0$ and the system does not have a unique solution.
options.B: $k=1$ and the system has a unique solution.
options.C: $k=-1$ and the system has a unique solution.
options.D: $k=-1$ and the system has infinitely many solutions.
